Number of studies.evidence_source: The present study sought to extend this body of research by examining the association between the Consider subscale of the ACSS (which directly measures future interest and likelihood in having cosmetic surgery, rather than attitudinal dispositions about cosmetic surgery) and body appreciation, media influence, and respondent weight status and age.

section_summary.extract_value: This Introduction reviews trends in cosmetic surgery and prior research linking willingness to undergo cosmetic procedures with variables such as body image, media exposure, and demographics. It states that the present study examined associations between the ACSS Consider subscale (interest in cosmetic surgery) and body appreciation, media influence, BMI, and age, and predicts that lower body appreciation, greater internalization of media influence, higher BMI, and older age will be associated with greater consideration of cosmetic surgery.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: "In recent years, developed countries have witnessed a dramatic increase in the number of cosmetic procedures being performed annually..." and "The present study sought to extend this body of research by examining the association between the Consider subscale of the ACSS ... and body appreciation, media influence, and respondent weight status and age. ... it was predicted that participants with less body appreciation, higher internalisation of media influence, a higher body mass index (BMI), and older age would report greater consideration of cosmetic surgery."
